newsitem.title: MEXICO: Pemex confirms two crude sales to US West Coast.
newsitem.headline: Pemex confirms two crude sales to US West Coast.

text.p: Adrian Lajous, head of Mexico's oil monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex), on Tuesday confirmed that two one-time shipments of Maya crude were sold to clients on the U.S. West Coast in the last month.
"Pemex has sold two shipments to California," Lajous told a news conference. He said the sales were not part of a longer contract.
Traders on the West Coast said in mid-July that Pemex had sent trial shipments to California. This marked the first shipments from Pemex to the U.S. West Coast in seven years.
"We are working in all markets to widen our number of clients," Lajous said. He declined to give further information on future markets the oil giant was aiming to tap.
Maya is Pemex's heaviest grade of crude. The oil company usually only sells crude for contracts of at least one year, but traders said an exception was made in these trial shipments.
